prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts the corner of a room from a reclining viewpoint, where the left wall converges with the right wall at a dark vertical corner seam roughly 2.5 to 3 metres ahead of the camera wearer. In the lower-right foreground, the camera wearer's bare feet (about 1.2 to 1.5 metres away, just beyond arm's reach) and the edge of a bed or mat (extending from within arm's reach at roughly 0.8 metres out to 1.5 metres) appear very bright, while on the left wall an electrical switchboard and small shelf-mounted speaker (about 1.5 to 2 metres away, to the left of and slightly closer than the television) are brighter than the wall-mounted TV screen (about 2 to 2.5 metres away, above the foot of the bed). Across the five frames, the camera angle stays nearly stationary while the bright silhouettes of the feet shift slightly and in frame 5 one foot extends upward while the other lowers, partially occluding the lower wall near the corner. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly isolates the foreground protrusion of the raised feet against the shadowed lower wall and captures the continuous planar depth gradient of the two walls meeting at the corner. However, the map looks unreliable along the far-left edge where the wall and speaker are over-brightened to nearly the same depth value as the foreground bed, and it flattens small wall fixtures like the upper coat hooks into the background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the wall-mounted `tv` in the middle-left region across all five frames (roughly 2 to 2.5 metres in front of the camera wearer and about 0.3 metres to the right of the wall speaker), while leaving the surrounding walls, hooks, switchboard, and speaker unsegmented in black. Almost everything in the scene is out of arm's reach except the near edge of the bed in the lower right, and no other people are present in the room, though small animated figures appear on the TV screen facing various directions without looking at the camera wearer. Across frames 1 to 4, the `tv` mask remains steady in position, and in frame 5 the camera wearer's raised foot and the adjacent bed edge in the lower-right corner (roughly 1 to 1.5 metres away) are segmented as `person` and `keyboard`, with the rest of the wearer's body and the bed partly out of view below the bottom frame edge. While the segmentation map provides a crisp boundary for the angled rectangular TV screen despite screen glare in the RGB image, it is largely unreliable for the lower-right foreground. Specifically, it fails to detect the camera wearer's feet in frames 1 to 4 and misclassifies the patterned bed mat as a `remote` in frame 2 and a `keyboard` in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, detecting zero body or hand keypoints anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, no full standing or seated people are visible in the room, and no hands enter the field of view within arm's reach of the camera wearer. The only human body parts present in the physical space are the camera wearer's own bare feet and lower legs stretched out at the bottom-right edge of the frame (roughly 1.2 to 1.5 metres away, pointing upward and away from the camera), along with small human figures displayed inside the TV broadcast about 2 to 2.5 metres ahead. Across the five frames, as the camera wearer's feet shift slightly and one foot lifts higher in frame 5, the pose map shows no response or skeletal tracking. Consequently, the pose map contributes no spatial information beyond confirming the absence of upper-body or hand appearances, and it is unreliable for tracking heavily truncated egocentric lower limbs at the bottom margin of the view.
